name: Question 7
problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y-z=1 \\ 2x-3z=-2 \\ -x+y-2z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $42,$ then $x=$
worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system to reveal the coefficients:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+5y+(-1)z=1 \\ 2x+0y+(-3)z=-2 \\ (-1)x+1y+(-2)z=6.\end{aligned}
$$

We start by writing the determinant of the coefficients matrix, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|=42.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find ${D}_{x}$, we replace the first column by the right-hand side of the system, and calculate the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 6 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0+3)-5(4+18)-(-2-0) \\  & =3-110+2 \\  & =-105.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying Cramer's rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{-105}{42}=-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
